newsitem.title: USA: Ashland clears Nigerian development plans.
newsitem.headline: Ashland clears Nigerian development plans.

text.p: Ashland Inc said Tuesday its board has approved the development plan for the Okwori field offshore Nigeria.
"Our partner Total SA has also approved the plan. The next step is to obtain approval from the Nigerian National Petroleum Co," chief executive Paul W. Chellgren said.
He said production from Vermilion 410 in the Gulf of Mexico "reached 16.5 million cubic feet a day net to our interest" by the end of December.
Ashland Monday reported the begining of production there.
"We anticipate reaching maximum production in February when four additional wells from Vermilion 389 are brought on stream," Chellgren said.
He said Credit Suisse First Boston is assisting in the previously announced evaluation of strategic alternatives for Ashland Exploration Inc.
"A number of options have been studied, and we are well on our way to being in a position to make a recommendation to our board," Chellgren said.

The company said previously it wanted to complete any resulting business transaction before the end of calendar 1997, subject to regulatory approvals, tax rulings and market conditions. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
